title: "Day 25 — practise the complete workflow"
---

## Today's purpose

There is no new statistical method today. Use the time to practise the actions
you want to be dependable in later biology practicals: locate measurements,
check them, make a useful figure, explain variation, and produce a report that
another person can open and reproduce. Written examination design is outside
these teaching materials.

Choose the station where you need practice first. Everyone should eventually
complete the file recovery, R recovery, and interpretation checks. Use reference
pages freely: fluency includes knowing where to find an explanation.

## Station 1 — find and inspect the laboratory files

Download a fresh copy of [lab-data.zip](../downloads/lab-data.zip) and locate it.
In your shell workspace, inspect the archive, extract it into a new folder, read
the README, locate the sample manifest, and find the treated records. Before
running a pipe, predict how many matching records it should count.

Save an extract named `treated-samples.txt`, then locate it in a file manager.
Explain what `>` changed and whether the source manifest was modified. Package
the extracted folder into a new archive placed outside it; list the archive and
confirm the text extract was included.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint: the small vocabulary is enough

Use `pwd`, `ls`, `cd`, `unzip -l`, `unzip … -d …`, `less`, `grep -F`, `wc -l`,
and `zip -r`. Check the [terminal reference](../reference/terminal.qmd). The
manifest has two treated records; its header is not one of them.
:::

## Station 2 — repair a small R analysis

The following is deliberately broken code shown as text. Do not copy it into a
working report unchanged. Find at least three problems, then write a corrected
version in `recovery.R` in your project root:

```text
seedling <- read_csv("seedlings.csv")
seedlings <- mutate(seedlings, growth_mm = final_mm + initial_mm)
mean(seedlings$Growth_mm)
```

Consider package loading, file location, object names, case, and the meaning of
growth. Confirm the repaired calculation using P01: initial length 25.7 mm,
final length 44.3 mm. Save a labelled plot without changing raw data.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## A working repair

```r
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
seedlings <- read_csv("data/seedlings.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
seedlings <- seedlings |>
  mutate(growth_mm = final_mm - initial_mm)
mean(seedlings$growth_mm)
```

P01 grew 18.6 mm. The original used a wrong relative path, inconsistent object
names, addition rather than subtraction, and inconsistent column case. It also
did not establish that `readr` and `dplyr` were loaded in this session.
:::

## Station 3 — explain before calculating

Write a sentence responding to each situation. No new test is required.

1. One treated plant has 100 cells measured; one control plant also has 100.
   A student says there are 100 independent replicates per group. What is wrong?
2. Two groups have the same mean but one has twice the SD. What can you say
   about their observations?
3. A missing biomass value is replaced with zero. Why can that change the
   biological meaning of the analysis?
4. A treatment-minus-control estimate is 3 mm with a 95% interval of −2 to 8 mm.
   Does this establish no effect?
5. An unknown sample gives absorbance greater than the largest calibration
   standard. What should happen before reporting its concentration?
6. A fitted leaf-area/mass slope is positive. Does it prove that changing area
   experimentally will produce the same change in mass?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Compare your reasoning

1. There is only one independent treated and one independent control plant;
   cells within them do not supply independent treatment allocation.
2. Spread differs even though the means match. Equal means do not imply
   identical observations or distributions.
3. Unknown biomass and genuinely absent biomass are different observations.
   Zero invents a value and can shift the mean, SD, and comparison.
4. No: the interval includes zero and effects in both directions. Explain the
   range of compatible values rather than declaring equality.
5. Flag it as beyond range; dilute and remeasure using the assay protocol.
6. No: this is an observational association. Other plant properties may vary too.
:::

## Station 4 — your complete report

Return to the report from day 23 or one that still needs work. Starting from a
fresh session, render it without running console code first. Check that it has:

- A biological question and an independent experimental unit.
- The input filename, measurement units, and missing-data account.
- A readable plot of observations and a small relevant summary.
- An appropriately directed comparison or a line fit, if the question needs it.
- An interpretation with size, variation or uncertainty, and a limitation.
- Relative input paths, all required code, and an HTML output you can locate
  beside the source or in the documented `reports/` output folder.

If these work reliably, use the time to repeat them on an earlier dataset rather
than adding another statistical method. Discuss with a peer which parts would
change for a new biology practical and which parts would stay the same.

## Station 5 — local and remote, when available

Identify the computer and folder behind an SSH session, locate a supplied file,
disconnect, reconnect, and find it again. Locate the designated shared folder
through remote desktop and transfer one output to your laptop. If access is
still pending, record this as an outstanding practical skill; completing local
stations does not complete the remote-access task.

## Your handover to the next biology course

Save `reports/next-lab.txt` with a short workflow you can reuse: where to store
raw data, how to open a project, which checks to make, how to choose a figure,
and how to render and back up your report. Include one question you would ask a
lab teacher before analysing a dataset, such as “what was independently assigned
to treatment?” or “what do blank cells mean?”

**Before you finish:** locate the final report, source, input, and backup without
using a recent-files menu. Keep the [reference pages](../reference/r.qmd) and your
working project template for later practicals.
